title: Certificates of Deposit: Funding, Term Dates and Lapse of an Unfunded Certificate
content:
One of Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit does not begin to run on the day it is opened. It begins on the day its opening deposit posts. This page sets out how that day fixes the term dates, and what happens to a certificate whose opening deposit never arrives.

## Funding fixes the term

The certificate is funded, and moves from applied status to active status, on the business day its opening deposit posts. That posting day is the term start date. The maturity date is the date the tier's number of calendar months after the term start date; where the resulting month has no day with that number, the maturity date is the last day of that month.

When the opening deposit comes from the customer's own PCB checking account or PCB savings or money market account, that account is debited for the same sum, and the account must be owned by the same customer as the certificate.

## Funding window and lapse

Every tier gives the same window for the opening deposit:

| Tier | Calendar days allowed for the opening deposit |
|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 10 |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 10 |
| 12-Month Certificate | 10 |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 10 |
| 36-Month Certificate | 10 |
| 60-Month Certificate | 10 |

A certificate that is still in applied status once that many calendar days have passed since it was opened is closed as unfunded. The clock starts from the opening date recorded on the certificate. The count is in calendar days, and the first day counted is the one after the opening date. The lapse falls due on the date that lies the window's number of days after the opening date, and on any later date; that boundary date itself is included.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Opening date | Date under review | Day count | Still in applied status? | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 March | 11 March | day 9 | yes | Not yet lapsed; the deposit may still post. |
| 2 March | 12 March | day 10 | yes | Lapse due; the certificate is closed as unfunded. |
| 2 March | 14 March | day 12 | yes | Lapse due. |
| 2 March | 12 March | day 10 | no, funded on 5 March | Nothing lapses; the term started 5 March. |

## Worked example of term dates (hypothetical)

- Assume a tier whose term is six months. The opening deposit posts on 31 August, so the term start date is 31 August. Six calendar months on there is no 31 February, and the maturity date becomes the last day of February.
- Assume a tier whose term is twelve months. The opening deposit posts on 15 January; the maturity date is 15 January of the following year.
